data.content_ref: inline:The relation asserts a non-linear cognitive-calibration mechanism but its refutation condition is mis-specified relative to the neighbourhood integration task. The 'refuted if' clause tests only a narrow empirical outcome — whether the non-linear path yields a measurable accuracy increase over a linear compliance path. That test cannot actually falsify the proposed INTEGRATION relation, because the integration claim is structural (friction as a necessary phase of calibration), not merely instrumental (friction yields better accuracy). A non-linear path could fail the accuracy test yet still integrate the node by establishing a dependence or shared mechanism between corrective friction and calibration. Conversely, a linear path could match accuracy while bypassing calibration entirely, so the refutation condition neither protects nor tests the integration relation itself. The counterexample condition thus tracks an instrumental benchmark, not the substantive relation it claims to refute.
